title: Slow-cooker chicken thighs with tomatoes and olives
subtitle: Italian-style braised chicken in a rich tomato sauce
excerpt: Bone-in chicken thighs braised slowly with tinned tomatoes, kalamata olives, and capers. The sauce is thick and flavourful; the chicken stays very moist and falls off the bone.
sourceNotes: Braised chicken with tomatoes and olives is a Mediterranean staple found in Italian and Greek cooking. The method draws on classic Italian pollo alla cacciatora tradition documented in Marcella Hazan, The Classic Italian Cook Book (1973).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps well in the fridge for up to 3 days. The flavour improves overnight.

content.text: Bone-in chicken thighs are the right cut for this recipe. They stay moist and flavourful after hours of braising, unlike chicken breast which dries out. The thighs release their fat and gelatin into the sauce, thickening it and giving it body. By the time the dish is ready, the meat will slip from the bone cleanly.
The olives and capers add salt and sharpness that balance the sweetness of the tomatoes. Do not add extra salt until you have tasted the finished dish; the olives and capers often do enough.
Serve with pasta, polenta, or crusty bread to catch the sauce.

Place {{chicken-thigh}} chicken thighs in the slow cooker. Add {{onion}} sliced onion, {{garlic}} of sliced garlic, {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes, and {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree. Add {{olives-kalamata}} of kalamata olives, {{capers}} of capers, {{bay-leaves}} of bay, {{oregano-dried}} of dried oregano, and {{chilli-flakes}} of chilli flakes if using. Add {{red-wine-vinegar}} of red wine vinegar. Stir to combine.

Set the slow cooker to LOW and cook for 5 to 6 hours. The chicken is ready when it is very tender and beginning to pull away from the bone. Discard the bay leaves. Taste before adding any salt; the olives and capers may have provided enough.

rows.cause: Kalamata olives and capers are both high in salt. Some brands are saltier than others.
rows.fix: Rinse the olives and capers in cold water before adding next time. Add a pinch of sugar to balance the flavour.

rows.cause: Tinned tomatoes release liquid during cooking. Bone-in chicken also releases some liquid.
rows.fix: Remove the lid and set to HIGH for 30 minutes to reduce. Alternatively, transfer the sauce to a saucepan and reduce separately.

rows.symptom: The chicken skin is soft and unappealing
rows.cause: Skin does not crisp in a moist slow cooker environment.
rows.fix: Remove the skin before cooking or after cooking before serving. Skinless thighs are best for this recipe.

rows.cause: The combination of tinned tomatoes, red wine vinegar, and olives is quite sharp.
rows.fix: Stir in a small pinch of sugar or a teaspoon of honey to soften the acidity.

content.text: Braised chicken with tomatoes and olives sits at the heart of southern Italian and Greek home cooking, where olives and olive oil are constants. The cacciatore style, literally hunter style, is named for the bold flavours that would travel well on a long day out. The slow cooker version is a practical modern answer to the same principle.
